claims.text: K depletion (common): frequent serum K monitoring; treat as needed w PO or parenteral potassium chloride
claims.quote: Potassium (K+) depletion, common in metabolic acidosis, should be identified through frequent serum K+ monitoring and treated as needed with oral or parenteral potassium chloride.

claims.text: Hemodialysis: for renal failure and sometimes for ethylene glycol, methanol or salicylate poisoning
claims.quote: Hemodialysis is required for renal failure and sometimes for ethylene glycol, methanol, or salicylate poisoning.
claims.locator: Treatment of Metabolic Acidosis › Cause treated

claims.text: Type 4 RTA: a few pts need mineralocorticoid replacement (fludrocortisone 0.05 to 0.2 mg PO once/day); caution, may worsen HTN, HF or edema
claims.quote: Type 4 RTA Hyperkalemia is treated with volume expansion, dietary potassium restriction, and potassium-wasting diuretics (eg, furosemide 20 to 40 mg orally once or twice/day titrated to effect). Alkalinization is often unnecessary. A few patients need mineralocorticoid replacement therapy (fludrocortisone 0.05 to 0.2 mg orally once/day, often higher in hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism); mineralocorticoid replacement should be used with caution because it may exacerbate underlying hypertension, heart failure, or edema.

claims.text: RTA bone dz: vitamin D (eg, ergocalciferol 800 IU PO once/day) and PO Ca supplements may be needed to help reduce skeletal deformities from osteomalacia or rickets
claims.quote: Vitamin D (eg, ergocalciferol 800 IU orally once/day) and oral calcium supplements (elemental calcium 500 mg orally 3 times/day, eg, as calcium carbonate, 1250 mg orally 3 times/day) may also be needed to help reduce skeletal deformities resulting from osteomalacia or rickets.
